Operator ran the diagnostic commands and shared output interactively; investigation continued live rather than stopping. Confirmed hypothesis (1) from the prior phase: the plan workflow had by then reached COMPLETED (via backlog-status on the correct Temporal workflow_id, not the campaign UUID -- the assistant's earlier guidance to use the campaign UUID was wrong and caused two spurious 500s, corrected). Step 5 (backlog-start) then hit a SEPARATE, real, systemic bug: 'CLAUDE_HEALTH_STALE' -- operations/repository.py's _provider_blockers() requires a QuotaSnapshot under 5 minutes old, but QuotaRefreshWorkflow (the only writer) is scheduled every 30 minutes (confirmed via `temporal schedule list`: last run 21 min ago, next in 8) -- so this preflight fails ~83% of the time by design. Worked around it live via `temporal schedule trigger --schedule-id engineering-quota-refresh` (a legitimate, safe, standard Temporal operation) to force a fresh snapshot, then retried backlog-start within the fresh window. THAT THEN FAILED IMMEDIATELY, revealing the real headline finding: ExistingGitHubBacklogLoopWorkflow's second activity call, `backlog.register_run` -- the exact step NEW-16's own fix added -- is not in ControlActivities._allowed_steps in EITHER the deployed release or this git repo's HEAD, so it fails with a non-retryable 'unknown or invalid control step' error on every single fresh execution. Every existing test mocked the activity dispatcher and never caught this -- tonight's attempt was the first genuine end-to-end exercise of NEW-16's fix since it was written. Confirmed the consequence directly: retrying backlog-start against the same campaign returned the exact same stale cached STARTED operation rather than a fresh attempt, reproducing NEW-16's ORIGINAL bug exactly (no Run row was ever written, because the workflow crashed before reaching the try/except that writes one). Campaign defef39e-b0ae-4a36-8863-dd59f08e960c is now permanently burned, joining 3a363acd and c405b4d7. FIXED (git-only): added 'backlog.register_run' to _allowed_steps, plus a new AST-based regression test (test_every_literal_step_a_workflow_calls_is_a_registered_activity) that checks every literal step name any workflow calls against the real dispatcher's registered steps -- confirmed it fails without the fix and passes with it, closing this entire bug class going forward, not just this one instance. 769 tests, ruff/mypy clean. NEW-16's real_status downgraded to OPEN_CONFIRMED_WORSE: it was never actually functional, in git or in production, until this pass -- and still isn't deployed. The CLAUDE_HEALTH_STALE scheduling mismatch is recorded but not yet fixed or filed as its own numbered finding -- flagged for the operator to prioritize.

Operator: 'yes fix it' (CLAUDE_HEALTH_STALE). Filed as NEW-17. Root cause: QuotaRefreshWorkflow's 30-minute schedule (scheduler.py) and _provider_blockers()'s 5-minute staleness threshold (operations/repository.py) were independently hardcoded in two different modules, never checked against each other -- failed preflight ~83% of the time by design. Fixed properly, not just patched: added workflows/schedule_intervals.py as the single source of truth for QUOTA_REFRESH_INTERVAL (30 min) and CONNECTIONS_REFRESH_INTERVAL (15 min); scheduler.py now references it instead of an inline literal; operations/repository.py derives its staleness threshold as QUOTA_REFRESH_INTERVAL + a 10-minute buffer instead of an independent number, so the two can never silently drift apart again. Updated the one existing test asserting staleness at 10 minutes (no longer stale under the corrected ~40-minute threshold) to 45 minutes. Added a new test asserting the actual configured schedule interval has real margin under the actual configured threshold, not just that the constants are related by construction. 770 tests, ruff/mypy clean. Not deployed -- same deploy-review gate as NEW-16's fix applies.

Deployed NEW-18's fix to both hosts (commit 207288a), verified active/zero restarts. Retried musematic fresh (campaign 5e307f4c, --max-items 4) -- ownership acquisition was clean (no lingering lock from the earlier crashed campaign, confirming the register_run-in-try fix genuinely releases ownership on failure).
